papers.title: Bayesian Dark Knowledge
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of Bayesian parameter estimation for deep neural networks, which is important in problem settings where we may have little data, and/ or where we need accurate posterior predictive densities, e.g., for applications involving bandits or active learning. One simple approach to this is to use online Monte Carlo methods, such as SGLD (stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics). Unfortunately, such a method needs to store many copies of the parameters (which wastes memory), and needs to make predictions using many versions of the model (which wastes time).   We describe a method for "distilling" a Monte Carlo approximation to the posterior predictive density into a more compact form, namely a single deep neural network. We compare to two very recent approaches to Bayesian neural networks, namely an approach based on expectation propagation [Hernandez-Lobato and Adams, 2015] and an approach based on variational Bayes [Blundell et al., 2015]. Our method performs better than both of these, is much simpler to implement, and uses less computation at test time.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该方法将贝叶斯后验压缩为单网络，可迁移至有限元代理模型的UQ，但未涉及仿真采样或力学约束。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address FEA surrogate modeling, does not handle physical constraints, does not apply to implant or biomechanics design, and lacks any experimental validation in engineering contexts.

summary_zh.motivation: 将贝叶斯神经网络后验预测密度蒸馏为单一紧凑网络
summary_zh.method: 用SGLD采样后验，训练学生网络匹配预测分布
summary_zh.result: 在多个基准上优于EP和变分贝叶斯方法
summary_zh.validation: 在标准分类和回归数据集上对比验证

summary_en.motivation: To compress a Monte Carlo approximation of the posterior predictive density into a single neural network for efficient Bayesian inference.
summary_en.method: Distill the predictive distribution from an ensemble of SGLD samplers into a compact student network.
summary_en.result: Achieves better predictive performance than EP and variational Bayesian approaches on several benchmarks.
summary_en.validation: Numerical experiments on standard classification and regression datasets.

papers.title: Enhancing Sparsity of Hermite Polynomial Expansions by Iterative Rotations
papers.abstract: Compressive sensing has become a powerful addition to uncertainty quantification in recent years. This paper identifies new bases for random variables through linear mappings such that the representation of the quantity of interest is more sparse with new basis functions associated with the new random variables. This sparsity increases both the efficiency and accuracy of the compressive sensing-based uncertainty quantification method. Specifically, we consider rotation-based linear mappings which are determined iteratively for Hermite polynomial expansions. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the new method with applications in solving stochastic partial differential equations and high-dimensional ($\mathcal{O}(100)$) problems.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文的方法论可用于提升生物力学代理模型中的不确定性量化效率，但缺乏对植入物设计约束的处理。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not handle constraints or optimization, lacks any biomechanics or implant design context, and does not apply to finite element surrogate modeling.

summary_zh.motivation: 提高高维随机问题中不确定性量化的计算效率
summary_zh.method: 通过迭代旋转寻找新随机变量基，增强Hermite展开的稀疏性
summary_zh.result: 在随机PDE和高维问题中提升了压缩感知方法的精度和效率
summary_zh.validation: 通过随机偏微分方程和高维数值算例验证

summary_en.motivation: To improve the efficiency of uncertainty quantification for high-dimensional stochastic problems by enhancing sparsity in polynomial expansions.
summary_en.method: Iterative rotation-based linear mappings are applied to identify new random variable bases that yield sparser Hermite polynomial expansions.
summary_en.result: The proposed method increases both the accuracy and efficiency of compressive sensing-based uncertainty quantification on stochastic PDEs.
summary_en.validation: Effectiveness is demonstrated on stochastic partial differential equations and high-dimensional (O(100)) benchmark problems.

papers.title: AlSi12 in-situ alloy formation and residual stress reduction using anchorless selective laser melting
papers.abstract: Rapid melt pool formation and solidification during the metal powder bed process Selective Laser Melting (SLM) generates large thermal gradients that can in turn lead to increased residual stress formation within a component. Metal anchors or supports are required to be built in-situ and forcibly hold SLM structures in place and minimise geometric distortion/warpage as a result of this thermal residual stress. Anchors are often costly, difficult and time consuming to remove and limit the geometric freedom of this Additive Manufacturing (AM) process. A novel method known as Anchorless Selective Laser Melting (ASLM) maintains processed material within a stress relieved state throughout the duration of a build. As a result metal components formed using ASLM do not require support structures or anchors. ASLM locally melts two or more powdered materials that alloy under the action of the laser and can form into various combinations of eutectic/hypo/hyper eutectic alloys with a new lower solidification temperature. This new alloy is maintained in a semi-solid or stress reduced state throughout the build with the assistance of elevated powder bed pre-heating. In this paper the ASLM methodology is detailed and investigations into processing of a low temperature eutectic Al-Si binary casting alloy is explored. Two types of Al powders were compared; pre-alloyed AlSi12 and elemental mix Al + 12 wt% Si. The study established an understanding of the laser in-situ alloying process and confirmed successful alloy formation within the process. Differential thermal analysis, microscopy and X-Ray diffraction were used to further understand the nature of alloying within the process. Residual stress reduction was observed within ASLM processed elemental Al + Si12 and geometries produced without the requirement for anchors.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文涉及铝合金SLM的残余应力降低，与生物医学植入物的多孔结构、应力遮挡或疲劳性能无关。
llm.why_not_core: The paper does not cover porous structures, stress shielding, fatigue testing, or surface roughness for biomedical implants; it focuses on residual stress reduction in AlSi12 alloys without any biomedical or osseointegration context.

summary_zh.motivation: 减少SLM成型过程中由热应力引起的几何变形和支撑结构需求。
summary_zh.method: 采用无锚点选择性激光熔化(ASLM)方法，通过原位合金化形成低凝固温度合金。
summary_zh.result: ASLM工艺成功减少残余应力，无需支撑即可成型几何结构。
summary_zh.validation: 通过差热分析、显微镜和X射线衍射验证合金形成和应力降低。

summary_en.motivation: To reduce geometric distortion and eliminate the need for support structures in SLM by minimizing thermal residual stresses.
summary_en.method: Anchorless Selective Laser Melting (ASLM) is employed, which uses in-situ alloying of multiple powders to form a low-solidification-temperature alloy that remains stress-relieved during the build.
summary_en.result: ASLM successfully reduces residual stress and enables fabrication of geometries without anchors.
summary_en.validation: Validation was conducted via differential thermal analysis, microscopy, and X-ray diffraction to confirm alloy formation and stress reduction.

summary_zh.motivation: 识别强直性脊柱炎患者全髋置换术后异位骨化的危险因素
summary_zh.method: 回顾性分析患者临床资料与影像学结果
summary_zh.result: 男性、术前已有异位骨化等为显著危险因素
summary_zh.validation: 基于临床队列数据的统计分析

summary_en.motivation: To identify risk factors for heterotopic ossification after total hip arthroplasty in patients with ankylosing spondylitis.
summary_en.method: A retrospective review of clinical and radiographic data from a cohort of patients.
summary_en.result: Male gender and preoperative heterotopic ossification were significant predictors of postoperative HO.
summary_en.validation: Statistical analysis of clinical data from patient records.

summary_zh.motivation: 探索减少全髋置换术后隐性失血的方法。
summary_zh.method: 临床对照试验，局部应用氨甲环酸加稀释肾上腺素。
summary_zh.result: 局部应用可显著减少术后隐性失血。
summary_zh.validation: 通过临床指标和输血率验证。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate a method to reduce hidden blood loss after total hip arthroplasty.
summary_en.method: A clinical controlled trial with topical application of tranexamic acid plus diluted epinephrine.
summary_en.result: Topical application significantly reduced postoperative hidden blood loss.
summary_en.validation: Validated by clinical outcomes and transfusion rates.
